B: Hi! Hello, can you hear me okay?
A: Loud and clear. Gareth. How are you doing?
B: I'm good, thanks, I'm Hannah. How are you?
A: Not bad at all. Bit damp. The car park at work's flooded again, so I've been paddling to my van all day. Where are you, then?
B: Exeter. Well, Pinhoe, just on the edge. I'm doing a PGCE, primary, so I'm on placement in a Year 1 class at the moment.
A: Oh, are you? My daughter teaches primary. Ellie, she's in Leeds. You remind me of her a bit, actually, in your photo. She's got the same look of someone who's been up since six doing laminating.
B: [laughs] That's literally me. Sorry, that's quite accurate. I was laminating at the kitchen table last night. Does she like it?
A: She loves it. Shattered every Friday, mind, but she loves it. She's always telling me what the kids have said.
B: They say the best things. One of mine told someone this week my ponytail looks like a horse's bottom.
A: [laughs] Brutal. They don't hold back, do they? I do school visits for work, and you get a quiet one at the back, and then you show them a newt and suddenly they won't stop talking.
B: Oh, what do you do?
A: Countryside ranger, for the council up in Darwen, Lancashire. Moorland, woodland, a reservoir walk. Bit of path repair, bit of dry-stone walling, and the school groups. Best bit of the job, them.
B: That sounds amazing. I'd love to take a class somewhere like that. We do Dartmoor with the dog at weekends, me and my mum and dad.
A: Dartmoor, lovely. What sort of dog?
B: Cocker spaniel. Biscuit. He rolled in something absolutely disgusting on Sunday, we had to drive home with all the windows down.
A: [laughs] We had a collie. Old lad died two years ago, and I'm still working on Helen to get another one. She says she's not ready. I think she means she's not ready for the hair on the settee.
B: Aw. Spaniels are good, just saying. Erm, but they do roll in things, so.
A: I'll leave that bit out when I tell her. Have you got a job lined up for after?
B: Not yet. I'm applying for ECT posts round Devon. I really want to stay close to home, so I'm kind of crossing my fingers. My mum keeps saying it'll be fine. She's a practice manager at a GP surgery, so she's very, like, it'll get sorted.
A: You're joking. Helen does that. Practice manager, part-time.
B: No way! Do you think they're all like that?
A: [laughs] Probably. They run the world, them lot, nobody notices. Do you do anything outside teaching, or is it just plans and laminating?
B: Netball on a Tuesday. And I help with the kids' group at church on Sundays, which is sort of how I got into teaching in the first place.
A: Tuesday's my choir night. Church hall, tenor. We're doing a Christmas concert in a few weeks, so it's all rehearsals. I go to the parish church most months, not as regular as I should.
B: Oh, I love that. I join the church choir at Christmas sometimes, but I'm not very good. I'm more of a musicals in the car person. I've seen Wicked twice.
A: Twice? Go on, then. Is it worth it?
B: It's so worth it. You'd like the songs, honestly, if you're a singer. Erm, maybe not the green bit, but
